title: Introducing Knowledge for Mastra Agents
summary: Give your agents a knowledge base to search, read, and update.
body_markdown:
You can now give your agents company-wide context using[Knowledge](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/overview) , a shared store of documents, policies, or decisions organized as pages. Knowledge works directly with[signals](https://mastra.ai/docs/signals/overview) , Mastra's context engineering primitive. Signals bring the right knowledge into an agent's context and keep it current while the agent runs. Agents can also search, read, and write Knowledge with tools, in the scopes they have access to.


Your browser does not support the video tag.A Knowledge scope in Studio, where an agent answers from its pages and a coding agent turns a pinned proposal into a pull request, recorded back on the page as a note.


LLMs know a lot, but they don't know everything. When agents are asked questions, they fall back on training data — which is often wrong. The real answers are usually spread across multiple systems, or in one person's head: why a feature was built a certain way, which policy applies, or what the team has already tried. Giving agents a knowledge base to read and learn from makes them more capable of understanding and answering questions that are specific to you, your business, or product.


You could already give agents context using instructions,[RAG](https://mastra.ai/reference/rag/overview) ,[skills](https://mastra.ai/docs/skills) , or tools that query APIs and databases, but they're usually read-only, and when information changes, each would need manual intervention to update. With Knowledge, an agent can not only read information but update it too, allowing it to learn and self-improve over time.


You can[seed Knowledge](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/load-your-content) with your existing documents or by using[Mastra Connect](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/connect/overview) on Mastra platform. Knowledge importers are coming in the next release, letting you connect data sources like Notion, Confluence, Linear, Zendesk, and Fireflies more easily.


## Get started


Knowledge stores information as named markdown documents your agents can read, called[pages](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/overview#what-knowledge-is) . Each page lives in a[scope](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/scopes-and-access) , which decides which orgs, users, or conversations have read/write access.


Terminal


```text
npm   install   @mastra/core@latest   @mastra/server@latest   @mastra/libsql@latest
```


note


Requires` @mastra/core@1.82.0` or later, added in[PR #28353](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/28353) .


Create a` Knowledge` instance and declare its scopes with` knowledgeMemoryScopes()` , which sets up three scopes:


- ` org:` shared with everyone in an org.
- ` resource:` visible to one user.
- ` thread:` limited to one conversation.


Setting` tools: true` gives agents five[Knowledge tools](https://mastra.ai/reference/knowledge/knowledge-tools) :


- ` knowledge_search` finds pages and notes that match a query.
- ` knowledge_list` lists the pages in a scope.
- ` knowledge_read` reads a page.
- ` knowledge_page` creates or edits a page.
- ` knowledge_note` adds a note to a page.


src/mastra/knowledge/company-knowledge.ts


```text
import   {   Knowledge,   knowledgeMemoryScopes   }   from   "  @mastra/core/knowledge  "  ;


export   const   companyKnowledge   =   new   Knowledge  ({
id:   "  company-knowledge  "  ,
scopes: {   ...  knowledgeMemoryScopes  () },
tools:   true
});
```


Give the` Knowledge` instance to an agent using the` knowledge` option:


src/mastra/agents/company-agent.ts


```text
import   {   Agent   }   from   "  @mastra/core/agent  "  ;
import   {   companyKnowledge   }   from   "  ../knowledge/company-knowledge  "  ;


export   const   companyAgent   =   new   Agent  ({
id:   "  company-agent  "  ,
name:   "  Company Agent  "  ,
instructions:   /* ... */  ,
model:   /* ... */  ,
knowledge: companyKnowledge
});
```


Register the agent and Knowledge on your Mastra instance. Knowledge is stored in your configured storage provider, which adds its own` mastra_knowledge_*` tables the first time Knowledge is used:


- ` mastra_knowledge_pages` holds each page's name, description, and markdown body.
- ` mastra_knowledge_notes` holds the notes added to pages.
- ` mastra_knowledge_mentions` records the links between pages.
- ` mastra_knowledge_pins` holds pinned pages.
- Further tables track scopes, access, and recent activity.


src/mastra/index.ts


```text
import   {   Mastra   }   from   "  @mastra/core/mastra  "  ;
import   {   LibSQLStore   }   from   "  @mastra/libsql  "  ;
import   {   KNOWLEDGE_ROUTES   }   from   "  @mastra/server/server-adapter  "  ;


import   {   companyAgent   }   from   "  ./agents/company-agent  "  ;
import   {   companyKnowledge   }   from   "  ./knowledge/company-knowledge  "  ;


export   const   mastra   =   new   Mastra  ({
agents: { companyAgent },
knowledge: { companyKnowledge },
storage:   new   LibSQLStore  ({ id:   "  mastra-storage  "  , url:   "  file:./mastra.db  "   }),
server: { apiRoutes: [  ...  KNOWLEDGE_ROUTES] }
});
```


` KNOWLEDGE_ROUTES` turns on the Knowledge page in Studio, which shows every scope and page as a tree beside a graph of how the pages link. See[Knowledge in Studio](https://mastra.ai/docs/studio/knowledge) .


## Usage


Each call passes its scopes: an org, a user (` resource:` ), and a thread.


For a question, the agent searches and reads pages across all three scopes:


```text
await   companyAgent.  generate  (  "  What's our refund window?  "  ,   {
scopes: [  `  org:  ${  user.orgId  }`  ,   `  resource:  ${  user.id  }`  ,   `  thread:  ${  threadId  }`  ]
});
```


For updates, the agent writes the page to the scope that matches the request. "Save that for the team" writes to` org:`


```text
await   companyAgent.  generate  (  "  Our refund window is 30 days. Save that for the team.  "  ,   {
});
```


## Seeding Knowledge


Agents can only answer from what's in Knowledge, so you'll usually want content in place before they start. There are a number of ways to seed Knowledge with your existing content, covered in[Load your content](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/load-your-content) .


For more information and full configuration options, see:


- [Knowledge overview](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/overview)
- [Scopes and access](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/scopes-and-access)
- [Agents and tools](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/agents-and-tools)
- [Load your content](https://mastra.ai/docs/knowledge/load-your-content)
- [Knowledge in Studio](https://mastra.ai/docs/studio/knowledge)
- [Knowledge class reference](https://mastra.ai/reference/knowledge/knowledge-class)


Knowledge is in alpha. Its API may change between releases.
